policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Pure Greek word order between infinitive and pronoun; ASV 'could not speak unto you' fixes the English order regardless of which Greek sequence stood, so nothing in the verse distinguishes them.
σαρκίνοις ('fleshy') and σαρκικοῖς ('fleshly') are both rendered 'carnal' in ASV usage; the single word 'carnal' here does not separate them, and no note is attached.
ASV 'I fed you with milk, not with meat' joins the two members asyndetically; the RP καὶ οὐ would give 'and not with meat', and the ASV renders καί in such coordinations rather than dropping it.
ASV 'nay, not even now are ye able' renders ἀλλ᾽ οὐδέ as 'nay, not even'; οὔτε is a correlative 'neither' with no answering member here and would not yield the intensive 'not even'.
ASV names only two things among them, 'jealousy and strife'; the RP addition καὶ διχοστασίαι would require a third, 'and divisions', which the verse does not have.
ASV closes 'are ye not men?', rendering οὐκ ἄνθρωποί; the RP οὐχὶ σαρκικοί would read 'are ye not carnal?' as in v. 3, and ASV keeps 'men' distinct here.
ASV asks 'What then is Apollos?', the neuter Τί; the RP masculine Τίς would be 'Who then is Apollos?'

ASV names Apollos first and Paul second ('What then is Apollos? and what is Paul?'), which excludes the RP order r02; r00-base and r01 have identical wording and differ only in editorial punctuation, which the English cannot decide.
ASV answers with the bare predicate 'Ministers through whom ye believed'; the RP ἀλλ᾽ ἤ would add an adversative 'but' before 'ministers', which is absent.
ASV 'I laid a foundation' is a simple past rendering the aorist ἔθηκα; ASV renders the perfect τέθεικα as 'I have laid', and it keeps that tense distinction consistently.
ASV reads 'buildeth on the foundation' with no demonstrative; the RP addition τοῦτον would give 'on this foundation'.
ASV 'gold, silver' renders the simple nouns and the diminutive forms χρυσίον/ἀργύριον identically; r00-base and r01 differ only in punctuation. Nothing in the English separates the three.

ASV 'and the fire itself shall prove each man's work' has the intensive 'itself' answering τὸ πῦρ αὐτό; omission would leave 'the fire shall prove'. The attached note is an alternative_rendering about English word order and does not bear on this.

The variants differ only in the position of οἰκεῖ relative to ἐν ὑμῖν; ASV 'dwelleth in you' is the fixed English order either way. The note offering 'sanctuary' is an alternative_rendering for ναός and does not touch this unit.
ASV 'all are yours' requires a copula in English whether or not ἐστιν stood in the Greek, and the verse carries no italicized supply or note marking it as added.
